newsitem.title: USA: AT&T to start local service in Michigan.
newsitem.headline: AT&T to start local service in Michigan.

text.p: AT&T Corp said Monday it filed a tariff with the Michigan Public Service Commission to begin providing local telephone services in Grand Rapids, Mich., and other Kent County communities on Tuesday.

AT&T said it will initially process only a limited number of residential orders from the Kent County area until it is certain that operational interfaces with Ameritech Corp can handle expanded volume. Orders then will be processed from residential customers from throughout the state, AT&T said.

AT&T said it will initially serve consumers by reselling Ameritech local phone service. The service will provide customers with a single bill for long-distance and local service, and AT&T said it will offer economical pricing and 24-a-day customer service, the company said.
AT&T spokesman Thomas Hopkins said the tariff filed with the public service commission includes details on pricing and service. The commission earlier this year approved AT&T for local service.

Hopkins said basic monthly rates charged to residential customers will be comparable to those charged by Ameritech, at $10 for 50 outgoing local calls a month, and $12.80 for 400 outgoing calls a month.
Prices for other services, such as voice mail and call waiting, also will be comparable to Ameritech.

Hopkins said AT&T has not decided whether it will build its own local network in Michigan, and is studying several network options, including forming partnerships with other telecommunications providers and cable television companies.

AT&T also plans to introduce digital wireless service for Detroit area customers later this year, and the facilities installed for that service in the future could provide a backbone for a local telephone network, Hopkins said.
